title: PGP for portfolio optimization: application to ESG index family
summary: Conventional portfolio design assumes Gaussian returns, but asymmetric and heavy-tailed returns call for higher-order moments. The paper proposes a mean-variance-skewness-kurtosis model, optimised with parametrised polynomial goal programming (PGP), to build diversified portfolios.
keyFindings: PGP generates multiple portfolios that reflect investors' different preferences over the four moments.
Portfolios are compared through the empirical cumulative distribution of returns to help investors choose a weight set.
methods: Mean-variance-skewness-kurtosis optimisation with polynomial goal programming, applied to the S&P ESG index family.
